employer_type.prompt: What kind of employer offers the plan?
employer_type.help: Government and religious-organization plans follow different rules from private employer plans.

funding.prompt: Is the plan self-funded or fully insured?
funding.help: Self-funded (also called self-insured) means the employer pays claims and an insurance company only administers the plan. Your plan documents or HR department can tell you.

options.label: Fully insured by an insurance company

issued_state.prompt: Was the insurance policy issued in New Jersey?
issued_state.help: Your plan documents name the state. If your employer is based in another state, the policy may have been issued there.

purchase_channel.prompt: Where did you buy the plan?
purchase_channel.help: Get Covered New Jersey is the state-run marketplace (the New Jersey version of HealthCare.gov).

options.label: Directly from an insurance company, while living in New Jersey

medicare_kind.prompt: Which kind of Medicare is this?
medicare_kind.help: Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans are run by private companies and have their own plan name and card.

options.label: A Medicare Advantage plan from a private company
Original Medicare (the red, white, and blue card)

grandfathered.prompt: Do your plan documents say the plan is “grandfathered”?
grandfathered.help: Grandfathered plans are older plans that some federal appeal rules don’t fully cover. Most plans today are not grandfathered.

options.label: No, or it doesn’t mention it
